articles.title: Clamor en Ceuta: "Es normal que los futbolistas no quieran venir aquí... estamos en la mierda"
articles.standfirst: La afición caballa asegura que la situación de la ciudad autónoma afecta directamente al rendimiento del equipo.
articles.summary: La afición asegura que la situación de la ciudad autónoma afecta directamente al rendimiento del equipo.
articles.body: Ir al fútbol en Ceuta se ha convertido en algo mucho más profundo que acudir a un recinto deportivo. Es la oportunidad de mostrar, durante 90 minutos, el descontento de una ciudad con la situación que atraviesa. El Alfonso Murube ya es un lugar de comunión ceutí en el que, antes del partido, puedes leer en su videomarcador un mensaje claro: "Ceuta no se vende, Ceuta se defiende". Un mensaje que no entiende de colores, tal y como demostró el Celta Fortuna, que saltó al césped con una camiseta en la que se leía "Ceuta, estamos con vosotros". Justo antes del himno del conjunto caballa sonó el de España y la grada se tiño de rojo y amarillo. Si hay algo de lo que se sienten orgullosos en Ceuta es de ser españoles. "Estamos orgullosos de nuestra españolidad, pedimos que nos olviden. Los políticos nos han vendido, pero seguiremos adelante. Hemos sentido el apoyo del resto de España, pero estamos en la mierda", comentan varios aficionados en la previa del partido. Algunos de ellos tienen miedo. "Hay que venir aquí para verlo. Mi hija no puede salir a la calle y empieza el colegio el lunes", comenta a MARCA un padre de familia. Además, entienden la situación crítica del equipo en cuanto a los fichajes: "La situación está perjudicando claramente al equipo. Teníamos quince fichajes que no han querido venir. Pero es lo normal. ¿Cómo vas a venir con tu familia y tus hijos? Casi nadie quiere venir aquí. La situación es muy complicada. Nos perjudica a los ciudadanos y a los jugadores. Ellos también son personas y es normal que no quieran venir, lo entendemos", lamentan.

articles.title: Ceuta no quiere un Mundial con Marruecos: "No deberían ni jugarlo, han atentado contra nuestro bienestar"
articles.summary: La afición de la A.D. Ceuta cuestiona la organización del Mundial 2030 con Marruecos: "Yo los echaría. No se merecen un Mundial. Si la gente se va de su país no pueden organizar un Mundial. Alguien que no es cómplice de nuestro bienestar no puede organizar un Mundial con nosotros", aseguraba un joven aficionado en la previa del partido ante el Celta Fortuna.
articles.body: La afición de la A.D. Ceuta cuestiona la organización del Mundial 2030 con Marruecos: "Yo los echaría. No se merecen un Mundial. Si la gente se va de su país no pueden organizar un Mundial. Alguien que no es cómplice de nuestro bienestar no puede organizar un Mundial con nosotros", aseguraba un joven aficionado en la previa del partido ante el Celta Fortuna. La situación que ha provocado el país africano tiene muy irritados a los aficionados caballas: "Yo echaría a Marruecos de la candidatura. No entiendo cómo puede haber dudas. Tiene que ser el Mundial de España y Portugal. A Marruecos nada. No debería ni participar en el Mundial". Alguno propone decisiones más drásticas: "Si yo fuera España no jugaba el Mundial. Y que la FIFA decida qué hacer si la campeona del mundo dice que no juega".

articles.title: Michigan-Western Michigan ending explained: MAC accepts Big Ten's claim that 1 second was left on clock before Hail Mary
articles.summary: NBC officiating analyst Terry McAulay speculated that the replay center's clock was out of sync. The Big Ten claims it was synced.
articles.body:
The easy word for what happened at the end of No. 16 Michigan's win over Western Michigan is "controversial." That might not work, though, as everyone seems pretty unanimous on what happened.

With only a few seconds on the clock, Michigan attempted a 47-yard Hail Mary that fell incomplete as time seemingly expired. A replay review predictably ensued, with the Big Ten's replay center eventually deciding to put one second back on the clock.

Michigan's second Hail Mary attempt had a better outcome, with the Wolverines pulling off a wild 13-12 win .

However, anyone with the ability to pause and slo-mo the replay shown on television can tell you the clock clearly struck zero while the ball was in the air on the first attempt. The clock should have stopped as soon as Western Michigan safety Micah Davis touched the ball because he had stepped out of bounds. But, again, time expired while the ball was in the air, assuming the stadium clock displayed on broadcast was correct.

There should not have been a final play, as far as any outside observer can tell. It is rare that a blown call feels this obvious, this blatantly irreconcilable with the plain fact of a clock on a screen.

It's not just a bad call, it's a call so bad it leaves us wondering how it's even possible.

There is, however, a theory of what happened courtesy of NBC officiating analyst Terry McAulay. In the aftermath of the ruling, McAuley went through the replay with the broadcast booth and explained that while the NBC broadcast supposedly had the stadium clock synced up on its replay, the Big Ten's replay center might have had a different sync with its Hawk-Eye camera.

McAulay also said a producer confirmed that the stadium clock was in sync with the broadcasts.

"The ball isn't even close to touching the player when it goes to zero. Now their Hawk-Eye system apparently either was — had a different sync or whatever and they came up with one second when it touched the players. I don't see how that happened, assuming our clock is correct. It is clearly not touching the player. The ball is clearly still in the air when the clock goes to zero on our screen. So the Big Ten's going to have to tell a lot of us how did they get to one second on this play."

That is all speculation, but it at least adds some sort of logic to an irrational sequence of events. It would still make the outcome an outrage, as a clock at the Big Ten replay center in Rosemont, Illinois, would be overruling the clock in Ann Arbor.

McAulay was clearly 100% correct in one regard, though: The Big Ten had some explaining to do.

The conference did its best attempt later Saturday night, releasing a statement with an accompanying video of the discussion in the replay center. Naturally, the combination did little to help our understanding of what happened.

The full statement, with our emphasis added:

Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling. Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned. Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-a, "A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside a boundary line." and thus the clock is stopped.

Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling.

Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned.

Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-a, "A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside a boundary line." and thus the clock is stopped.

That would appear to pour cold water on the unsynced clocks theory, except the video shows the replay officials working with a clock that actually did show one second left when Davis touched the ball. Almost as if it was out of sync with the stadium clock.

The situation is no less bizarre with that statement, though the Mid-American Conference, Western Michigan's representative in this, did release its own statement saying video and audio provided by the Big Ten confirmed its explanation .

It's also possible NBC was incorrect about its clock being synced with the stadium clock.

We are operating in a world where there are three clocks at play here: the broadcast clock, the stadium clock and the replay center clock. It can't be denied there was a kink in the chain somewhere.

articles.title: Big Ten attempts to explain officiating review in Michigan's controversial Hail Mary win over WMU
articles.summary: College football didn't wait long to deliver its first game-clock dispute of 2026.
articles.body:
College football didn't wait long to deliver its first game-clock dispute of 2026.

During the first full Saturday of the season, Michigan beat Western Michigan, 13-12, on a 47-yard Hail Mary on the final play of the game — a play only made possible after a decision from Big Ten officials to add one second to the game clock.

Officials added the second after reviewing an incomplete Hail Mary attempt from Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood that sailed behind the end zone and out of bounds. In NBC's televised replay, the network's game clock graphic showed zeroes as the first player touched the incomplete pass, presumably ending the game.

However, NBC's replay was apparently not in sync with the actual game clock that officials in the Big Ten replay center used in its review, according to video the Big Ten released at 12:48 a.m. ET Sunday.

The league distributed a statement as well as audio and video of replay officials inside the Big Ten replay center in Chicago discussing the play and determining the ruling . The video that officials used showed one second on the clock when Western Michigan safety Micah Davis touched the ball out of the back of the end zone.

Clock graphics used on broadcasts do not always match the stadium clock as they are shot by a camera and then projected into an on-screen graphic. NBC officiating analyst Terry McAulay suggested this live during the broadcast.

"As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game block, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling," the Big Ten's statement read.

In the case of Saturday's play, the television clock potentially being a half-second off from the game clock made a difference.

As the stadium clock struck zeroes on the penultimate play, Western Michigan players burst into celebration before coach Lance Taylor and staff corralled them back on the sideline for the review. A couple of minutes later, officials announced that one second would be put on the clock.

Underwood took the snap and, this time, tossed his Hail Mary toward the goal line and into the outstretched arms of receiver JJ Buchanan, who fell into the end zone to elicit the unexpected: Michigan fans storming the field after beating their little in-state brother.

Another rarity unfolded minutes later, when Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna took the podium during the Broncos' postgame news conference to field questions about the end of the game.

"This football team deserves a second look if that's possible," Kavalhuna said.

His coach spoke to the media beforehand in a calm and composed manner. At the time of his news conference, Taylor said he had not seen video of the replay , but he had already received communication from MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher and expected to remain in contact with him.

In a statement, Steinbrecher said the league sought clarification on the play from the Big Ten, which provided video and audio of the replay that "confirmed the explanation provided to us."

"We can't control if there's a second left on the clock or not," Taylor said after the game. "We went out the first time and defended perfectly. The Hail Mary situation, I thought our guys did an excellent job [on the penultimate play]. When I looked at the clock, it was past zero before we touched [the ball]. I knew they would review it because it was the last play of the game. We did not defend it as well the second time."

Heartbreak for the Broncos was relief for Kyle Whittingham's Wolverines in his debut as head coach.

"The extra second was huge," he said. "As I watched the first Hail Mary end and the ball sail out of the back of the end zone, as I glanced at the clock, I was pretty certain there was one second on the clock. … This game will go down in Michigan history."

articles.title: El Real Madrid C se atasca en su debut
articles.standfirst: El filial de Marc Carrasco empató sin goles (0-0) en su estreno liguero ante el Atlético Albacete, con la puntería como asignatura pendiente y un providencial Illia como salvador bajo palos
articles.summary: El filial de Marc Carrasco empató sin goles (0-0) en su estreno liguero ante el Atlético Albacete, con la puntería como asignatura pendiente y un providencial Illia como salvador bajo palos
articles.body: El Real Madrid C echó a andar su nueva temporada en la Segunda RFEF, esta vez con Marc Carrasco en el banquillo, y lo hizo con un tropiezo en casa. Los blancos empataron sin goles ante el Atlético Albacete en un estreno en el que se encontraron con la falta de gol arriba como principal enemigo. Si el filial rescató un punto fue, en buena medida, gracias a un providencial Illia, que bajo palos se erigió en salvador con varias intervenciones de mérito para mantener su portería a cero. El encuentro arrancó con un intercambio de golpes en los primeros compases, aunque ninguno de los dos conjuntos logró ser letal en las áreas. El C mejoró de forma notable tras el cambio de extremos ideado por Carrasco, con Viega pasando a la derecha y Gabri Valero a la izquierda. Fruto de esa reordenación llegó una buena ocasión de Liberto en una internada por el costado zurdo. Ya en la segunda mitad, el técnico movió el banquillo con la entrada de Álvaro Ginés por Zinebi en punta, y el recién ingresado protagonizó la primera acción de peligro clara para los blancos en un mano a mano que, sin embargo, acabó invalidado por fuera de juego. La igualdad se mantenía, con Illia atento bajo palos para detener una peligrosa falta de Rosell lanzada desde el balcón del área. El partido dejó también el debut de los fichajes Bellosillo y Rajado, que saltaron al campo junto a Lacosta. El tramo final ganó en emociones. Manex avisó con un disparo peligroso desde fuera del área, al que Illia respondió, esta vez en la portería contraria, deteniendo un mano a mano con valor de gol a Fran Gómez. Acto seguido se vivió una de las acciones más feas del choque, con un codazo de Javi Navarro a Gabri Valero que solo se saldó con amarilla, cuando pudo haber sido expulsión. En los compases decisivos, el Madrid C no halló con claridad la vía para generar ocasiones y desnivelar la balanza. Apenas una llegada desde atrás de Yeremaiah, que se marchó muy alta, inquietó la meta rival. El filial, con más voluntad que pegada, tuvo que conformarse con un punto en un estreno liguero que dejó la sensación de que el gol será la asignatura a trabajar por los de Carrasco. Real Madrid C: Illia; Guille González, Aimar, Sotres, Liberto; Beto, Manex Rezola; Gabri Valero, Carlos Díez, Viega; Zinebi. También jugaron: Álvaro Ginés, Rajado, Bellosillo, Lacosta y Yeremaiah. Entrenador: Marc Carrasco. Atlético Albacete: Ramos; Jota, Vicente, Velilla, Scott; Javi Navarro, Diego; Fran Gómez, Fabio, Rosell; Tomás. También jugaron: Busto e Idowu. Entrenador: Ricardo Fajardo. Árbitro: Francisco de Asís Vidal.

images.caption: Marc Carrasco, técnico del Real Madrid C. REALMADRID.COM

articles.title: Arnau Ortiz, baja 'inesperada' para Liverpool
articles.standfirst: El extremo arrastra una sanción ¡desde agosto de 2024!, cuando fue expulsado en la fase de clasificación de la Conference League con el Sląsk Wroclaw polaco
articles.summary: El extremo arrastra una sanción ¡desde agosto de 2024!, cuando fue expulsado en la fase de clasificación de la Conference League con el Sląsk Wroclaw polaco
articles.body: Más allá de un Sorloth al que aún no se espera de vuelta (pese a que ya va para un mes desde que se lesionara aún permanecerá en la enfermería), Simeone tampoco podrá incluir en la lista de expedicionarios para Liverpool a Arnau Ortiz. Pese a que aguarda su estreno en la Champions, su anterior experiencia en Europa dilata una jornada más su presencia, pues arrastra una sanción... ¡desde agosto de 2024! Aunque ya han pasado dos años del que fuera su cuarto partido en competición continental, la UEFA mantiene el castigo sobre Arnau Ortiz, por entonces futbolista del Sląsk Wroclaw polaco. Fue tras un polémico partido de la fase de clasificación de la Conference League frente al St. Gallen en el que el extremo sería expulsado en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. De hecho, pese a ingresar al campo pasados los 100 minutos de juego, Arnau sería víctima del 'gatillo fácil' del colegiado, que ya había expulsado a un central, un delantero y a un integrante del cuerpo técnico local en pleno intento de remontada (el Slask llegó a ponerse 3-1 tras caer 2-0 en la ida). Así, primero sería amonestado por supuestamente simular una falta y a renglón seguido vería la segunda amarilla por protestar. La guinda a una polémica saldada con la eliminación tras anotar el cuadro suizo el 3-2 sobre la bocina. Una experiencia, en definitiva, que al margen del mal sabor de boca que dejó en Arnau su última presencia en competiciones europeas, prolonga ahora su 'penitencia' perdiéndose la visita del Atlético a Anfield. Un peaje, eso sí, que invita al catalán a esperar con 'sangre en los ojos' su posible estreno en la Champions frente al Manchester United el próximo 13 de octubre.

images.caption: ARNAU ORTIZ. ARABA PRESS

articles.title: Valencia - Barcelona en directo | Última hora de LALIGA EA Sports hoy, en vivo
articles.summary: Quería salir el Valencia pero Cubarsí da un paso hacia adelante y obliga a Danjuma a quedarse parado porque se metía en fuera de juego. ¡¡AL LARGUERO
articles.body:
Última hora del Valencia - Barcelona en directo:

¡¡Muuuuuuuuuuuuuy buenas tardes a todos y bienvenidos a otra apasionante jornada de LaLiga EA Sports en MARCA.com!! Viajamos a Mestalla , donde el líder puede dar el primer golpe encima de la mesa en la pelea por el título. Primera oportunidad para que los de Flick se queden solos al frente del liderato tras el tropiezo el pasado viernes del Real Madrid en el Villamarín.

El inicio arrollador del conjunto catalán podría dar un paso más de sacar hoy los tres puntos en Mestalla. Marcaría la primera distancia con Real Madrid y Betis , ahora mismo los principales perseguidores con nueve puntos. Con el debut en Champions ante el Feyenoord a la vuelta de la esquina, la duda radica en qué once presentará Hansi Flick esta tarde. Si rotará pensando en el compromiso europeo o, por el contrario, saldrá con todo su arsenal.

El Valencia, por su parte, vive un momento delicado con un ambiente crispado entre club y afición, donde la figura de Carlos Corberán se encuentra más discutida que nunca. El mal inicio, con un punto de nueve posibles y dos partidos en casa sin conocer la victoria, hacen presagiar otra tarde complicada en Mestalla de no dar la campanada y poner al líder contra las cuerdas.

Desde ya mismo os iremos contando todo lo que suceda en torno al partido de Mestalla: alineaciones oficiales, ambiente previo, datos y estadísticas... ¿Os animáis a vivirlo con nosotros? ¡Venga que eeeeeeeeeeeeempezamos!

articles.title: Borja Iglesias y Sebastián Cáceres, novedades en la convocatoria
articles.standfirst: Faye se queda fuera por decisión técnica y Febas sigue lesionado
articles.summary: Faye se queda fuera por decisión técnica y Febas sigue lesionado
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez facilitó la lista de 24 futbolistas cara al partido de este lunes en Getafe. Borja Iglesias y Sebastián Cáceres son las dos principales novedades. El campeón del mundo recibió el alta este domingo y entró directamente en la convocatoria. El máximo goleador céltico las dos últimas temporadas todavía no ha debutado en este campeonato. A su vez, Sebastián Cáceres se estrena en una convocatoria, apenas cuatro días después de su llegada y con apenas dos sesiones de entrenamiento. Por el contrario, Faye -uno de los fichajes de esta temporada- es descarte técnico. Tampoco entra en la lista el futbolista del Celta Fortuna, en dinámica de primer equipo, Andrés Antañón, que el pasado jueves fue titular ante la Real Sociedad. Sigue siendo baja por lesión, Aleix Febas. Por lo demás, vuelve a la lista, como tercer portero, Iván Villar, que recientemente perdió a su madre. En la lista continúa el futbolista del filial, Hugo Burcio.

articles.title: Matarazzo: "Oyarzabal ha recuperado bien y, como todos, está muy bien para mañana"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de la Real está satisfecho de como está evolucionando su equipo en estas primeras jornadas y acudirá a Elche con el objetivo de lograr el segundo triunfo
articles.summary: El técnico de la Real está satisfecho de como está evolucionando su equipo en estas primeras jornadas y acudirá a Elche con el objetivo de lograr el segundo triunfo
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo está satisfecho de la mejoría que su Real Sociedad está teniendo a nivel defensivo y ahora espera que vuelva a ser ese equipo con muchas ocasiones en ataque para aprovechar algunas y ganar más partidos, empezando por el de mañana en Elche. Matarazzo ve al equipo recuperado del cansancio del jueves, en especial a Oyarzabal, y preparado para visitar mañana al Elche. “El equipo esta muy bien, he tenido muy buenas sensaciones en el entrenamiento, estamos con muchas ganas del partido de mañana. Y Mikel también está muy bien. Es verdad que terminó muy cansado el partido contra el Celta, él hizo un encuentro muy completo. Controlamos los números de Mikel y de todos los futbolistas, para evitar las lesiones, y además Mikel conoce muy bien su cuerpo”. El técnico txuriurdin está satisfecho de la progresión de su Real con el paso de los partidos. “Estoy contento con la evolución que el equipo ha ido teniendo en cada partido. Hemos concedido pocas ocasiones y hemos recibido pocos goles, si quitamos los cuatro del Real Madrid, solamente dos en tres partidos, lo que está muy bien”. El de Nueva Jersey ha explicado el porqué muchos de los jugadores del Sanse que entrenan a sus órdenes jugaron con el segundo equipo ayer y no irán mañana a Elche. “Creo que es muy importante para los jóvenes jugadores que jueguen. Algunos habían tenido menos minutos con nosotros en los últimos partidos, era bueno que tuvieran muchos con el Sanse. Marchal sigue porque está con mucha confianza, para mí incluso es una opción para salir de inicio mañana”. No ha dado ninguna pista sobre si Sarr y Fort pueden debutar mañana. “Están bien. Se han ido integrando bien, era importante que fueran conociendo como suelen ser los planes de partido y como se desarrollan, y ya están preparados para jugar, Mamadou es una opción para jugar mañana de inicio”. Zakharyan y Guedes han sido dos de los nombres propios de la rueda de prensa de Matarazzo. “Zakharyan tiene que ser paciente y entender que es importante salir con energía del banquillo, mientras que Guedes va mejorando físicamente y es posible que vaya jugando más”. También se le ha cuestionado un día más por Kubo y si ha hablado con él de su flojo inicio de curso. "Tuve una conversación muy agradable con Take después del partido. Bebimos un té verde japonés, soy un gran aficionado al té verde japonés, me encanta el Gyokuro, el Sencha, el Genmaicha... Hablamos sobre su situación, todos sabemos qué tipo de jugador es Take. Es un jugador capaz de marcar la diferencia en los partidos con asistencias, con goles o en los uno contra uno. También somos muy conscientes, y él también lo es, de que no está en su máximo nivel. Simplemente hablamos de lo que necesita de nosotros, de sí mismo y de lo que necesitamos juntos". Matarazzo tiene claro que ni él ni sus futbolistas deben fiarse de que el Elche aún ni haya ganado en esta LaLiga. “En la liga no hay rivales fáciles, da igual cómo vayan. Es un equipo muy ofensivo, con las ideas claras. Presionan, transitan, tendremos que estar muy concentrados y con ambición. Es cierto que tienen una defensa de cinco como el Celta, pero con un comportamiento diferente. Debemos a ir a tope, como contra todos los rivales de la liga”.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Live expanding to 2.5 hours to provide even more weekly start-sit advice

articles.title: Giráldez: “Tenemos que encontrar la estabilidad cuanto antes”
articles.standfirst: El técnico ve evolución en su equipo
articles.summary: El técnico ve evolución en su equipo
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez ve mejoras en su equipo, centrado tras la conclusión del mercado y espera que todo ello se plasme en el encuentro ante el Getafe, de gran exigencia. Getafe: “Primero tenemos un reto apasionante, al jugar contra uno de los mejores equipos a nivel de orden y defensivo de LaLiga y en un escenario complicado. Hace mucho calor, creo que tenemos un reto importante para esa evolución ofensiva que nos va a exigir estar muy bien para poder generar ocasiones de gol y goles. El Getafe es un equipo que suele alternar momentos de presión en bloque medio alto o de estar más en medio bajo y tenemos que adaptarnos a ambas situaciones, ser capaces de tener soluciones para hacer daño en esos dos posicionamientos” Ser pacientes: “Debemos tener paciencia y tranquilidad, tenemos que mejorar versiones individuales de ciertos jugadores. Tenemos que entender que están en un proceso de evolución como equipo, ese acoplamiento de ciertas piezas, ciertos mecanismos que estamos teniendo. Estoy tranquilo porque van a acabar llegando las ocasiones de gol y a partir de ahí llegarán los goles. Situaciones que históricamente nos ha costado los inicios de temporada y que hemos ido evolucionando y en ello estamos. El equipo lo detecta, lo sabe y lo va a acabar haciendo". Plantilla centrada: “Somos seres humanos y el mercado es información permanente y eso de alguna forma te tiene que afectar. Intentas que sea lo menos posible. Ahora todo el mundo está focalizado al 200% aquí y ojalá que nos sirva el partido de Anoeta de refuerzo, de construcción de lo que queremos ser como equipo. El día del Athletic dije que demostramos todo lo contrario a lo que yo quiero que seamos como equipo y en la 2ª parte de Anoeta, incluso en el arranque, salimos con otra mentalidad, con otra idea y seriedad, otro empaque y estuvimos en una versión más cercana de lo que queremos". Un nuevo mal inicio: “Creo que es responsabilidad mía. Si sumo mis años con el Celta Fortuna creo que hemos arrancado bien en uno de todos ellos. Tenemos que seguir evolucionando en arrancar y ser competitivos con resultados desde antes. Salvo la primera temporada mía que arrancamos en Primera y en la que hicimos 2 victorias en casa y a partir de ahí tampoco tenemos demasiados buenos resultados. El año pasado y este no hemos arrancado con los puntos que nos gustaría. El año pasado con partidos buenos en casa que no acabamos de convertir en puntos, este año con 2 buenos partidos fuera de casa que no convertimos en los puntos que nos gustaría y con 2 partidos en casa, uno raro ante Osasuna y uno muy malo ante el Athletic". Mejoras necesarias: “Tenemos que encontrar la estabilidad cuanto antes y ser capaces de sacar resultados. Hemos tenido la suerte de que esos dos años han acabado muy bien y por eso tenemos que ser exigentes pero también tener la paciencia que toca. Ojalá pudiéramos ganar todos los partidos, arrancar bien, estar bien todos los meses pero todos los equipos tienen procesos distintos en cuanto a rendimiento. Estoy seguro que LaLiga no acabará como está ahora a nivel clasificatorio. Tenemos que mejorar el nivel individual, el mío el primero. Tenemos que coordinarnos a nivel colectivo y el resultado nos dará autoestima, tranquilidad. Centrándonos en el proceso y a los jugadores los veo tranquilos, con ganas y que podemos ser competitivos contra cualquiera”.

articles.title: Dabo Swinney's Clemson Contract Buyout, Details Revealed After 41-Point Loss to Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: There was a time not long ago when Dabo Swinney was considered one of the best coaches in college football as his Clemson Tigers were consistently competing for national championships.
articles.body:
There was a time not long ago when Dabo Swinney was considered one of the best coaches in college football as his Clemson Tigers were consistently competing for national championships.

However, things continued to trend in the wrong direction Saturday during a 51-10 loss to Lane Kiffin and LSU, which brought Swinney's contract buyout situation under the spotlight.

Robby Kalland of CBS Sports reported Clemson would save $3 million by firing Swinney during the 2026 season instead of after it with a flat-rate buyout of $57 million compared to the $60 million for his total compensation starting in 2027. The buyout clause features a descending flat rate for the first five years, and this is the fifth year on his deal.

Yet Swinney's contract does not feature a mitigation clause, meaning the Tigers would be on the hook for the entirety of the buyout even if he took another job.

Such a mitigation clause saved Penn State a significant amount of money after it fired James Franklin.

He dropped his buyout from $49 million to $9 million and became Virginia Tech's coach after the Nittany Lions moved on, but Clemson wouldn't get that type of reprieve if Swinney found his next opportunity.

Despite the recent struggles for the Tigers, he likely wouldn't have to wait long to find that opportunity.

After all, Swinney led Clemson to the College Football Playoff national championship game four times in a five-year span from 2015 through 2019. He won the national title twice during that run and established the ACC program as one of the best in the sport.

Even when the Tigers fell short of those expectations the following three years, they still won double-digit games in 2020, 2021 and 2022.

Still, things have trended in the opposite direction of late, as Clemson lost four games in 2023 and again in 2024 before going an ugly 7-6 last year. Last year's Clemson team had nine players selected in the NFL draft with four of them going in the first two rounds, so talent didn't appear to be the issue.

"Swinney's Tigers were once perennial national title contenders and favorites to win the ACC, but as college football has changed in the NIL and transfer portal era, Swinney's stubbornness has seen the Tigers stumble off that perch atop the ACC," Kalland wrote.

With last year's struggles looming, Swinney was under plenty of pressure to bounce back in a high-profile showdown with LSU on Saturday. Instead, his team was blown out and managed just 105 passing yards to go with 40 yards on the ground at 1.5 yards per carry.

Clemson has not enjoyed as much success as many of its marquee-program counterparts in the modern era of college football, and that could eventually mean moving on from the winningest coach in school history if things don't turn around the rest of this season.

articles.title: Michigan's second-chance Hail Mary win over Western Michigan shows why football needs to overhaul the way it measures time on its game clocks
articles.summary: Football game clocks don't show tenths of a second. As every aspect of the game is dissected by instant replay, clocks need to be more exact too.
articles.body:
Michigan's win over Western Michigan and the Big Ten's ensuing explanation are further proof that it's long past time for the NFL and college football to use game clocks that show fractions of a second.

The No. 16 Wolverines beat the Broncos 13-12 on Saturday night on Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary to JJ Buchanan as time expired. It was an incredible throw and catch; Underwood fired a rocket as he was getting hit, and Buchanan went up in traffic to make a fantastic contested grab. But it's also a play that isn't getting the appreciation it deserves because of how the end of the game unfolded.

Underwood's throw was his second Hail Mary attempt. His first sailed out of the back of the end zone and didn't touch WMU's Micah Davis until there was no time remaining on the clocks that NBC viewers saw at home. As WMU celebrated, it was clear to anyone watching the game from their house or local sports bar that one of the biggest upsets of the season had just happened.

Officials declared that there was one second remaining on the game clock when Davis, who jumped from out of bounds, touched the football. Hours after the play was over, the Big Ten issued a statement explaining the decision and showing a video of the game clock synced to an angle of the play where you can't conclusively see exactly when Davis touched the football. However, it is clear from that footage that the Big Ten's official clock was still showing 0:01 after the ball made contact with Davis.

But just how many tenths remained in that final second when the ball hit Davis' hands? Were there three tenths? Just a singular tenth? We don't know. And that's a big problem with accepting the Big Ten's explanation at face value. A clock that shows fractions of a second could go a long way to not only disproving conspiracy theories stemming from Saturday night, but also in all other late-game timing rulings going forward.

In this case, the confusion appears to stem from a discrepancy between the clock on NBC and the official game clock. And it's a discrepancy that would be far easier to decipher in tenths of a second.

On the play before Michigan's first Hail Mary attempt, Underwood spiked the ball on first down. The spike came as Michigan got to the line with the clock stopped and 11 seconds remaining. After the spike, the NBC game clock showed eight seconds to go.

Following the play, the referee clearly announces to the crowd and the clock operator that the clock should be reset to nine seconds. That reset is reflected on the NBC ticker, as their clock changes to 0:09.

However, when Underwood takes the snap for the first Hail Mary, the ticker clock is already at 0:08 seconds. Anyone who watches football knows that it doesn't take an entire second for a shotgun snap to get to a quarterback.

As NBC repeatedly showed the replays of the Hail Mary with the clock superimposed on the screen, rules analyst Terry McAuley's only explanation for the addition of the second was if the clocks on the TV network weren't exactly in sync. It was an explanation that made even more sense the day after — and one that could much more easily be deciphered if football clocks showed tenths of a second.

On the current game clock, 0:01 could mean anything from 1.0 seconds to 0.01 seconds. It's a remarkably rudimentary time-measurement process in a game that's dissected frame-by-frame in instant replay. Replay officials can reasonably determine if a player's toe touched a blade of turf that's painted white and out of bounds. But they can't say for certain if a half-second remains on the clock or just two- or three-tenths.

If fractions were shown on the game clock Saturday — and the Big Ten's statement included a video of the entire play synced to the official game clock — it'd be much easier to figure out just how off the clock on TV was for those tasked with explaining the clock differences and those who are trying to understand them.

Adding tenths of a second to game clocks is hardly a new idea, either. In 2023, the Philadelphia Eagles made an NFL competition committee proposal for the game clocks to show tenths of a second within the final 30 seconds of each half. When that idea didn't pass, Philadelphia proposed it again in 2024 and expanded the scope to the final 60 seconds. That idea didn't pass, either.

It's time for the Eagles' idea to be revived, both in the NFL's competition committee ahead of the 2027 season and on the NCAA's FBS rules committee, too. Saturday night's game needs to be the impetus for change. It won't be an easy one, as game clocks in stadiums across the country will have to be replaced and reconfigured. But that's a small price to pay for more clarity.

articles.title: Birmingham City 2-2 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Jackson Tchatchoua's nightmare own goal earns point for Blues
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Wolverhampton Wanderers at St Andrew's on Sunday; Jackson Tchatchoua scored a chaotic own goal as spoils were shared.
articles.body:
All the goals in a thrilling derby came in the first half. Fer Lopez steered Wolves in front before Jay Stansfield levelled for Birmingham. There were questions over whether he handled it as he controlled the ball, but the finish was emphatic as he lashed it into the top corner.

Ladislav Krejci, making his first league appearance of the season, then headed Wolves back in front, before Tchatchoua inexplicably steered the ball beyond his own goalkeeper Jose Sa with a blind pass.

Both sides had chances to win it in the second half, but the golden opportunity fell to Adam Armstrong in the dying embers, who somehow struck the ball over from inside the box after being teed up perfectly by Lopez.

The key moments from a cracker at St Andrew's

3: GOAL! What a start for Wolves! A hectic opening and it's their star of the season so far who has given them the lead. Fer Lopez turns smartly on halfway and gives it to Jimenez. He the finds Gomes to his right, who crosses into the middle, where Lopez has continued his run to bury it from close range.

18: BIG SAVE! Wolves should be 2-0 up. Birmingham lose it deep in their own half and Jimenez feeds in Gomes. He is through on goal and tries to slot it past Beadle, but a big hand from the big goalkeeper puts it wide.

23: GOAL! Jay Stansfield LASHES Birmingham level. The Blues work it forward nicely. Roberts then clips one into Stansfield, who controls it brilliantly on his chest before smashing one past Sa from the angle. What a hit.

31: GOAL! Wolves are back in front! A corner comes in from Bueno which is headed on by Andre, and Krejci arrives to absolutely pelt a header into the back of the next from six yards.

36: GOAL! WHAT ON EARTH HAVE I JUST WITNESSED. Tchatchoua what have you done. A harmless ball is played back to the defender. And without looking he tries to hook it back to his goalkeeper. But Sa has come off his line, and the defender's ball passes him and ends up crossing his own line.

87: HUGE CHANCE TO WIN IT! Out of nowhere, Wolves have an unbelievable chance. Fer Lopez latches onto a long ball up the pitch and he plays Armstrong in. He just has to do his thing and slot it home past Beadle, but he launches it over the bar!

"There are mixed feelings because I'm proud of the performance. I thought they gave their all and I'll always be content with that, but I'm frustrated that we haven't managed to get the three points.

"I think there was probably enough in there. It was against a really good side. They obviously had their moments, but I thought we could have won it.

"They had a chance towards the end as well, to be fair, but we take a point. Again, it was an encouraging performance.

"You need the three points. Encouraging draws are a good thing, but you need the three points and that's what we've got to keep searching and pushing for."

"It is difficult to explain something like [the own goal]. I don't say anything. We have to stay together, all together. Mistakes happen in games. Today was a mistake, but we have to fight together.

"It is not because of Jack that we didn't win. We had [plenty of time] to score a third goal and win the game. We have to play better, but today was very difficult.

"Birmingham are a difficult team. They play directly, with the first ball and second ball all the time. They are a strong team and win a lot of duels.

"I think the referee allowed a lot of passes and play to continue, but it is one point for us. It is not what we want, but I am happy with one point."

articles.title: Fidalgo se sube al carro de Pellegrini
articles.standfirst: El asturiano disputó ante el Real Madrid sus primeros minutos en lo que va de temporada
articles.summary: El asturiano disputó ante el Real Madrid sus primeros minutos en lo que va de temporada
articles.body: La victoria del pasado viernes frente al Real Madrid dejó muchas noticias positivas para el Betis. Los verdiblancos pasaron página de la mejor manera posible de la dura goleada que una semana antes habían sufrido en el Ciudad de Valencia frente al Levante. Se reconciliaron a su vez con una afición algo molesta por lo ocurrido en el cierre del mercado de fichajes, con la salida de Pablo García y la no llegada de un pivote. Y al mismo tiempo, recuperaron para la causa a varios futbolistas llamados a sumar minutos de calidad en una exigente temporada, con Liga, Copa y Champions. Uno de ellos fue Álvaro Fidalgo. El asturiano, que adelantó su regreso de las vacaciones tras disputar el Mundial con la Selección de México como futbolista naturalizado, no había tenido minutos en ninguna de las tres primeras jornadas de Liga. Según anunció su técnico, sufría unas molestias en una rodilla que invitaban al cuerpo técnico a tener cierta precaución y no arriesgar dándole minutos si no era estrictamente necesario. Y a ello se unió lo ocurrido en las últimas horas de mercado, en las que su nombre fue protagonista. El exjugador del América recibió el interés de varios equipos de Primera, que con la llegada de Dani Ceballos y la negativa de Deossa e Iker Losada a salir, vieron la posibilidad de 'pescar' el río revuelto. Fidalgo, como jugador de club que es, se puso a disposición del Betis para lo que la Dirección Deportiva considerara necesario. Pero en la entidad tuvieron claro desde el principio que en ningún caso iban a forzar un movimiento de salida para un jugador como Álvaro, que apenas llevaba unos meses en el equipo, en que confían y con un comportamiento intachable. El viernes, ante el Real Madrid, club en el que se formó, Fidalgo tuvo sus primeros minutos de la temporada. Media hora en el terreno de juego para subirse al carro de Pellegrini y demostrar que puede y debe ser un futbolista muy útil para el equipo en las rotaciones. Una actuación repleta de dinamismo, buenos movimientos y acierto en el pase (13 buenos de 14 intentos, nueve de 10 en campo contrario) que completó con su entrega defensiva (dos duelos ganados) para frenar a los de Mourinho cuando buscaban la remontada. Con un centro del campo en el que aparecen nombres como los de Isco, Fornals o Lo Celso, el nivel de exigencia para jugar es altísimo. Pero el punto de vista del Ingeniero es otro: con tres competiciones por delante y semanas de hasta tres partidos, contar con tantos futbolistas de calidad es una ventaja a la hora de repartir titularidades, minutos, esfuerzos y descansos. Ahí, Álvaro Fidalgo debe aportar su granito de arena demostrando que el gran nivel que mostró en sus primeros partidos como verdiblanco, a su llega de México, puede darle muy buen rendimiento a un Betis cada vez más ambioso.

articles.title: Penn State WR Koby Hwoard says he is just getting started after Week 1
articles.summary: Penn State wide receiver Koby Howard showed why he was being hyped this offseason with a game-high receiving yardage total in Week 1 vs. Marshall.
articles.body:
After a summer of building hype for his potential on the field this fall, Penn State wide receiver Koby Howard delivered the goods in the season opener. Howard had a game-high 161 receiving yards in Penn State's 45-0 victory over Marshall on Saturday. His single-game performance exceeded his entire 2025 receiving yardage total, and he is just getting warmed up.

Howard wasted no time showing his value as a receiving target for starting quarterback Rocco Becht in the first quarter. Howard made an adjustment on the fly to help his quarterback out after it appeared the primary target was not going to be an option on the play. Howard slipped into an open spot on the field to haul in a catch and then let his legs do the rest of the work on his way to the end zone for a first-quarter touchdown.

"I was looking to set a run for someone else. I think it was [running back James Peoples], but he slipped, so Rocco held onto the ball, and I saw him holding onto it," Howard recalled in a postgame media session. "I knew the ball was supposed to be out earlier than that. So, then I knew it was time to go get open, and you know, I ran to an open spot and he hit me."

Howard's performance continued to shine on a day where Becht was doing well to distribute the football to all of his options. Becht completed touchdown passes to four different players, starting wiht Howard, but Howard continued to make some big plays with his hands to keep the offense moving in chunks. For Howard, the seaosn debut was rewarding, but it is far too early to get carried away with expectactions.

"I feel like today was just a test, but you know it really doesn't stop here," Howard said in his postgame media breakout session. "I've just got to keep proving myself and keep showing the coaches that they can trust me so that when those big moments come, they're ready to call my number."

Howard appeared in nine games for the Nittany Lions last season, with four starts. He recorded 7 receptions for 133 yards as a true freshman. Most of his significant playing time came following the mid-season firing of former head coach James Franklin. Howard quickly received rave reviews from Matt Campbell this offseason as the rising star made a point of showing what he can do in camp and practices.

"I went in there knowing that I had stuff to prove," Howard said. "I was showing the coaches that I could be trusted, and I really don't want to come off the field, honestly. So, it was just showing the coaches that I could do that and showing them that they could throw me the ball in the game."

"I think the sky is the limit for Koby Howard, and I'm really proud of him because, you were ready for this moment," Campbell said in his postgame press conference on Saturday. "Your shots come, the moment's going to come when you take advantage of it, and Koby's a guy that's worked so hard behind the scenes to take advantage of this moment, so I'm really happy for him."

Howard is already among the Big Ten receiving yardage leaders after just one game. Odds are he will not be putting up 150+ receiving yards per game this season, but it was refreshing to see a young wide receiver step up to make some plays when needed in the Penn State offense out of the gates of the new season. Howard and Penn State will face stiffer pass defenses later on this season, but he could get another chance to impress in Week 2 when Penn State visits Temple in Philadelphia.

articles.title: VAR image shows why Lamine Yamal’s goal was disallowed for Barcelona vs Valencia
articles.summary: By a toenail.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal opened the scoring for Barcelon a against Valencia on Sunday with a brilliant strike but was denied a second minutes later due to VAR.

The Barcelona star saw his effort ruled out for an incredibly tight offside call. The image released after the decision was made show just how marginal the decision was to chalk off Yamal's goal.

Barcelona did go on to score a second in the first half. Fermin Lopez made it 2-0 after 22 minutes as Hansi Flick's side made a great start to the match.

Yamal was named in the starting XI despite missing full training before the game due to a knock. Yet the teenager showed no signs of injury as he began the game in great shape.

The teenager now has three goals in four games so far this season for Barcelona in La Liga and seems to be playing with a smile on his face again.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark USA stats tracker: Updated game logs for Fever star at 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup
articles.summary: Clark won MVP honors during Team USA's 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup qualifying tournament. She'll look to repeat the feat when the Americans touch down in Ger...
articles.body:
The break in the WNBA season has done little to quell the attention placed on Fever supernova Caitlin Clark.

The third-year star has enjoyed a wondrous 2026, propelling Indiana to a postseason berth while reminding onlookers just how good she can be when fully fit. For some, the break will offer respite before the start of a grueling playoff run. For Clark and many of the league's best players, the 17-day break will be filled with more basketball.

Clark is one of the headliners for Team USA in the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. She'll look to dazzle in red for Kara Lawson's bunch, the latest iteration in a string of talent-laden sides to wash ashore at the tournament in years past. The U.S. has won four straight gold medals in the competition and enters the tournament unbeaten in its last 30 World Cup matches. With Clark steering the side alongside Napheesa Collier, Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart, the Americans look well-equipped to keep those glistening runs alive.

In March, Clark took part in Team USA's World Cup qualifying run. She was splendid in the five-game offering, averaging 11.6 points and 6.4 assists on 53 percent shooting en route to earning MVP honors. If that performance was any indication, Clark could author up some gems in Berlin.

The Sporting News is tracking Clark's performance during the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. Follow below to keep up to date on the numbers behind Clark's major international tournament debut.

articles.title: Ceballos, Lo Celso y Diego Conde, en la lista de Pellegrini frente al Lille
articles.standfirst: El utrerano se estrena en una lista tras su regreso al Betis; Abde no se recupera a tiempo
articles.summary: El utrerano se estrena en una lista tras su regreso al Betis; Abde no se recupera a tiempo
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini, técnico del Betis, ha dado a conocer este domingo la lista de convocados de su equipo para el partido de la primera jornada de la Fase de Liga de la UEFA Champions League que los verdiblancos disputarán el martes frente al Lille, en Francia. Una citación en la que la una de las principales novedades es el utrerano Dani Ceballos, quien después de cuatro entrenamientos con el grupo ya está en condiciones de sumar sus primeros minutos en su nueva etapa con el club heliopolitano. Además de Ceballos, el Ingeniero puede contar ya para este partido con Giovani Lo Celso y Diego Conde. El guardameta madrileño sufrió una lesión en un hombro en la pretemporada y aún no había podido estrenarse en ninguna convocatoria en partido oficial con el Betis. El argentino regresó lesionado tras el Mundial, pero también está en condiciones de sumar minutos. Se quedan fuera Aitor Ruibal, que sigue con su proceso de recuperación, Diego Llorente, que sufrió el viernes la fractura de los huesos propios de la nariz en el partido ante el Real Madrid, y Abde, que tampoco pudo estar ante los de Mourinho por una gripe. Tampoco viaja Iker Losada por decisión técnica. El Betis volará a Francia mañana a primera hora de la mañana en vuelo chárter. A las 18.15 horas está programada la rueda de prensa oficial de Manuel Pellegrini en el Decathlon Arena, una comparecencia en la que estará acompañado por Álvaro Valles. Y desde las 19.00 horas el equipo se ejercitará en el escenario del partido. Este primer duelo de la Fase de Liga de la Champions para los verdiblancos está programado para el martes desde las 21.00 horas. articles.title: Five stats tell story of LSU football's dominant win over Clemson
articles.summary: LSU football secured an emphatic Week 1 victory over Clemson on Saturday night. Here are five stats that tell the story of the win.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's debut exceeded all expectations. Under the lights in Death Valley, LSU beat Clemson 51-10. LSU's offense moved the ball at will, while the defense was stifling. At one point in the second half, LSU had more touchdowns than Clemson had first downs.

Sam Leavitt threw an interception on the second play of the game, setting up Clemson in scoring position. That was the only good moment Clemson had all night. LSU responded by forcing a three-and-out and holding Clemson to a field goal.

After the pick, Leavitt was electric. He ran for 113 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 9.4 yards per carry. He added 230 yards and a touchdown through the air. Safe to say, Leavitt put to rest any concerns about last year's foot injury.

Here are five stats that define LSU's dominant win over Clemson.

LSU had 38 first downs; Clemson only had 8

Winning football games requires moving the ball. You do that by earning first downs. LSU did that at an elite clip on Saturday night. Clemson? Not so much.

Perhaps no stat puts this game in perspective more than LSU racking up 38 first downs while holding Clemson to eight. Most of Clemson's came in garbage time, too, when the game was already out of hand. Clemson went into the half with just one first down.

LSU had 300 passing yards and 300 rushing yards

Kiffin's offense was as advertised. The group was efficient, explosive, and balanced. LSU finished the game with 335 yards through the air and 309 yards on the ground. That's a sign of an offense firing on all cylinders.

LSU played clean football in every phase. Leavitt gained a large chunk of LSU's rushing yards on QB scrambles, but RB Dilin Jones ran for 113 yards in his LSU debut, too. As a team, LSU averaged 5.3 yards per carry. It's good advice not to overreact after Week 1, but I feel good saying LSU's run game is much better than it was in 2025.

Clemson's offense only averaged -0.47 EPA/play, according to GameOnPaper.com. That's a 0th percentile performance. This was an elite outing from Blake Baker's defense.

Clemson scored only because LSU's offense turned it over in the red zone and later allowed a garbage-time touchdown as time wound down in the fourth quarter. This was the most dominant LSU defense we've seen in a few years.

Clemson's success rate was 29% and Dabo Swinney's group averaged 3.02 yards per play. Both marks were among CFB's worst in Week 1.

There's a reason LSU paid up to land Sam Leavitt, the top-ranked quarterback in the transfer portal. The talent was on display on Saturday night.

Leavitt was dynamic with his legs. There were times when Clemson applied pressure, but Leavitt was elusive, often turning what would have been sacks into first-down scrambles. Leavitt had six runs of 10+ yards and forced three missed tackles, per PFF.

LSU's passing game could have been a bit cleaner at times, but that's expected with a QB making his first start in a new offense with several new players. Still, LSU did a good job scheming open receivers and Leavitt racked up 230 yards through the air.

LSU's defense got after it. Baker's unit was disruptive all night, posting a 29% havoc rate. The highlight havoc play came late in the first quarter, when LSU defensive end Jordan Ross dropped into coverage, picked off Clemson QB Christopher Vizinna, and followed a brigade of LSU defenders into the end zone for six. Ross had a career night, posting four pressures and a sack to go along with the pick.

Princewill Umanmielen delivered in his LSU debut, too, sacking the quarterback twice. Whit Weeks and TJ Dottery each notched four stops from the linebacker position. Weeks had a key tackle for a loss in the first half to stop Clemson on third down.

articles.title: Eibar 3-0 Granada | Resumen LaLiga Hypermotion
articles.summary: Nadie cuenta con el Eibar para el ascenso, pero ha comenzado el curso al mismo nivel que terminó la temporada pasada, en la que sumó 46 puntos en la segunda vuelta. Y eso son palabras mayores. 9 puntos de 12 posibles y un liderato provisional que no deja de ser anecdótico por mucho que ilusione a la parroquia armera. Iván Gil, Adu Ares y Guruzeta fueron los autores del incontestable triunfo del equipo de Jokin Aranbarri ante un Granada que cosechó el primer traspiés del curso.
